newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines' Ramos warns about partisan politics.
newsitem.headline: Philippines' Ramos warns about partisan politics.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos on Thursday urged presidential hopefuls to set aside partisan politics and focus on consolidating the economic gains achieved in recent years.

"Partisan politics has a way of diminishing our sense of nationhood and our sense of national accomplishment. We cannot -- and must not -- allow it to distract us..." Ramos said in his Independence Day speech in Cavite, just south of Manila.
The speech was delivered a day after three major opposition parties forged an alliance to challenge the ruling party in the 1998 elections.
The grand opposition alliance includes Vice President Joseph Estrada and Senator Edgardo Angara, who both are seeking the presidency.
Ramos said politicians should unite to uplift the poor, who comprise 70 percent of the population. The benefits of the steady economic growth of the past five years have yet to reach the poor.
"It will take very little to undo our accomplishments. If we give in to disunity, to pettiness, to the claims of short-term profit for a few over long-term gain for the many," he added.

The presidential race is well under way one year before the election with two Cabinet secretaries, four senators and the House speaker expressing interest in succeeding Ramos, whose six-year term ends in June 1998.
So far the presidential hopefuls have been engaging in minor word wars, a prelude to a campaign period that officially starts early next year.
